get.summary: Read the support inboxes the person works in on OpenVibe.Chat (docs/platform.md): the inboxes, each one's conversations (waiting first) and messages, and its saved replies; the owner also exports ever
get.description: **chat.inbox.read** (public): Read the support inboxes the person works in on OpenVibe.Chat (docs/platform.md): the inboxes, each one's conversations (waiting first) and messages, and its saved replies; the owner also exports every conversation (JSON or CSV). Visitors' messages are people's words to a team, so an app sees only inboxes its person works in, and the person's own role decides the rest (the export is the owner's).

chat.send-request.v1.title: ChatSendRequest
chat.send-request.v1.description: chat.send-request@1: what a sender hands OpenVibe.Chat to post a chat line (chat.message.send). From a browser, a frame on WS /ws/chat of type chat in the room the socket joined (the text is trimmed; empty or longer than 6000 characters is dropped, the channel's own max_message_length is enforced after that; a line starting with ! or / is a command, not a message). From Live's bridge, POST /internal/live/calls: a chat.live_bridge.write batch in which every op that sends a message (a chat or dm frame, db saveChatMessage, deployNotice) also needs chat.message.send; without it that op alone is refused. From a first-party service, POST /internal/chat/messages: one line (or one DM) that Chat stores, broadcasts to the room (with mirror, also to global chat and the streamer rooms), reads aloud (tts) and answers with the real id; applied once per (caller, key), the same key with another body gets 409.

reply_to_id.description: Id of a visible message in the room this replies to (parseInt; an unknown or deleted parent is ignored).

auto_delete_minutes.description: Delete the line after this many minutes (clamped to Chat's minimum and maximum; ignored where the channel turned viewer auto-delete off).

voiceChannelId.description: The voice channel the sender is in, echoed on the broadcast.

boot.description: Live's boot id; placeholder message ids are mapped per boot.

op.description: A ChatServer method, a bridge-only op, or db (an allow-listed chat-table write named by args[0]).

ref.description: Live's placeholder id for the row this op inserts.

key.description: Idempotency key, scoped to the caller and to this route.

is_global.description: Default: true when there is no stream and no channel.

auto_delete_at.description: When Chat deletes the line (a date Chat parses).

mirror.description: Also send the line to global chat and the streamer rooms.

dm.description: Send a direct message from user_id instead (no room, mirror, tts or frame; 403 if either blocks the other, 404 if either is unknown).

tts.description: Read the line aloud in its room (needs stream_id or channel_user_id).

frame.description: How the broadcast shows the sender.

first_chat_key.description: Whose first chat in the channel this is (user:, anon: or ext:); default from user_id or anon_id.

chat.send-result.v1.title: ChatSendResult
chat.send-result.v1.description: chat.send-result@1: what chat.message.send answers. On WS /ws/chat nothing is acknowledged directly: the stored line is broadcast as a chat frame to the room (the sender included; channel lines also reach the homepage global feed), and a refusal (banned, slow mode, held for IP approval, a channel rule, not saved) is a system or error frame to the sender alone. On POST /internal/live/calls, the batch result: one entry per op, in order, where a message op without chat.message.send is { ok: false, code: capability.denied }. On POST /internal/chat/messages: { ok: true, id } with the room (stream_id, channel_user_id, first_chat) or the DM (conversation_id, to_user_id), or chat.ingress-ack@1's error ({ ok: false, error }).

username.description: Display name, or the anonymous id.

core_username.description: The immutable login handle; null for an anonymous sender.

role.description: The sender's role, anon for an anonymous sender.

is_global.description: true for homepage global chat (no stream, no channel).

message.description: The parent's text, cut to 100 characters.

vip_badge.description: The channel's VIP member badge, when cached; otherwise a chat_vip_badge frame follows.

first_chat.description: Room only, since 1.2.0: true when this is the sender's first message in this channel's stream (Chat's stream_first_chats), so Live can welcome them without reading its own copy; absent on a DM and from an older Chat.

chat.sound-asset-request.v1.title: ChatSoundAssetRequest
chat.sound-asset-request.v1.description: chat.sound-asset-request@1: the body of POST /internal/chat/sounds/asset on OpenVibe.Chat (capability chat.sounds.write): after OpenVibe.Live's asset sync uploaded a channel sound to OpenVibe.Media, the asset is written back onto Chat's channel_sounds row id. Writing the same asset again is a no-op; an unknown id is 404. Answers chat.ingress-ack@1.

chat.sounds-result.v1.title: ChatSoundsResult
chat.sounds-result.v1.description: chat.sounds-result@1: the answer of GET /internal/chat/sounds on OpenVibe.Chat (capability chat.sounds.read). ?channel_owner_id answers { count } (a channel's custom sounds, for Live's channel readiness); ?pending_asset=1 answers { sounds } (rows with no media_asset_id yet, which Live's asset sync uploads to OpenVibe.Media and writes back with POST /internal/chat/sounds/asset). A failure is chat.ingress-ack@1's error.

command.description: The trigger word (no leading '!'), lowercased: the sound's name.

url.description: Where Chat keeps the audio file (its on-disk path).

media_url.description: The file's OpenVibe.Media URL; null until Live's asset sync uploaded it.

media_asset_id.description: The OpenVibe.Media asset id; null until uploaded.

chat.stats-request.v1.title: ChatStatsRequest
chat.stats-request.v1.description: chat.stats-request@1: the body of POST /internal/chat/stats on OpenVibe.Chat (capability chat.stats.read): one count over chat_messages, for the stats OpenVibe.Live shows without reading its own copy of Chat's tables (home and SEO stats, admin dashboard, star of the day, VOD and recap cards, stream analytics, top chatters, AI slogans). kind site counts all of chat; user one person's messages (user_id); stream one stream's messages, chatters and soundboard plays (stream_id); channel-top the top chatters, of one stream (stream_id) or one channel (channel_user_id), or of all chat when neither is given; site-daily one row per UTC day in [since, until), zero-filled, a kind that takes only since and until. since and until bound chat_messages.timestamp, epoch ms, until exclusive. Deleted messages are never counted. Loopback only, service token.

user_id.description: Live user id; required for kind user.

stream_id.description: Live stream id; required for kind stream.

channel_user_id.description: The broadcaster whose channel room it is (chat_messages.channel_user_id).

since.description: Count messages at or after this instant (epoch ms).

until.description: Count messages before this instant (epoch ms).

limit.description: How many top chatters (channel-top); Chat's default is 10.

chat.stats-result.v1.title: ChatStatsResult
chat.stats-result.v1.description: chat.stats-result@1: the answer of POST /internal/chat/stats (chat.stats.read). site, user and stream answer messages (non-deleted chat_messages rows) and chatters (distinct COALESCE(user_id, anon_id, source_platform || username)); stream also answers sounds (soundboard plays); channel-top answers top_chatters, most messages first; the kind site-daily is answered by chat.site-daily-result@1, not here. A failure is chat.ingress-ack@1's error ({ ok: false, error }).

user_id.description: Live user id; null for an anonymous or relayed chatter, counted by name.

display_name.description: From Chat's copy of the user (ctx_users); null when unknown.

chat.ticket-conversation.v1.title: ChatTicketConversation
chat.ticket-conversation.v1.description: chat.ticket-conversation@1: one conversation between an OpenVibe.Help ticket and one calling service, keyed by the ticket id and the service, carrying one posted message. The person side reads and answers it through Chat's person APIs (POST /api/chat/send needs a person's session); a service-side author (Help's agent worker, staff tooling) posts here with a service token, which is why the write needs the chat.ticket.write capability rather than the person send route. author_kind says who wrote the message (`person`, `agent` or `staff`), author is that author's subject, body is the text, and created_at is when the message was written.
chat.ticket-conversation.v1.$comment: Additive optional fields may extend this v1 contract.

ticket_id.description: The OpenVibe.Help ticket this conversation belongs to. Together with `service` it keys the conversation: one conversation per (ticket id, calling service).

service.description: The Contracts manifest id of the calling service (e.g. `help`, `ai`), the service token's principal. Together with `ticket_id` it keys the conversation, so two services on one ticket get two conversations.

author_kind.description: Who wrote the message: the ticket's `person`, an `agent` (a service acting for one, e.g. Help's AI worker), or `staff` (a human on the service's team).

author.description: The author's subject: `user:<id>` for a person, or the service/agent subject that posted on its behalf. Never a display name.

created_at.description: When the message was written (the author's clock; Chat keeps its own ordering).

message.author: user:usr_01JAB2C3D4E5F6G7H8J9K0MNPQ
message.body: My export from yesterday is missing the last day of records.

chat.timeline-result.v1.title: ChatTimelineResult
chat.timeline-result.v1.description: chat.timeline-result@1: the answer of GET /internal/chat/timeline on OpenVibe.Chat (capability chat.analysis.read): non-deleted chat_messages of one channel (channel_user_id) or stream (stream_id) counted per bucket between since and until (epoch ms), bucket_ms wide, for OpenVibe.Live's AI moments, chat spikes and activity. Empty buckets are left out; buckets are oldest first. max_id is the highest message id in the window, null when none. A failure is chat.ingress-ack@1's error.

chat.vibe-ask-request.v1.title: ChatVibeAskRequest
chat.vibe-ask-request.v1.description: chat.vibe-ask-request@1: a first-party service asks Vibe, OpenVibe's assistant, on a person's behalf (Vibe by voice: OpenVibe.Bot passes what the person said after their machine's call word). Chat keeps it in the person's own Vibe chats, one chat per source ("Voice on <machine>"), and answers with Vibe's reply, which counts against the person's daily allowance like any of their Vibe answers. POST /internal/chat/vibe/ask, capability chat.vibe.ask, loopback only.

subject.description: The person Vibe answers, as the calling service vouches (Bot: the machine's owner, with voice on for that machine).

id.description: The source's stable id (the machine's device id): one chat per source.

name.description: What to call it in the chat's name (the machine's name).

idempotency_key.description: The caller's id for this ask (Bot: device id and the voice_ask id): asked again, the same answer, once.

chat.vibe-ask-result.v1.title: ChatVibeAskResult
chat.vibe-ask-result.v1.description: chat.vibe-ask-result@1: Vibe's answer to a chat.vibe-ask-request@1. `answered` carries the reply (plain text, Markdown stripped, for speech); `refused` says why nothing was asked (Vibe resting, the person's daily allowance spent). `url` is the Vibe chat that keeps the question and the answer.

chat.vibe-deliver-request.v1.title: ChatVibeDeliverRequest
chat.vibe-deliver-request.v1.description: chat.vibe-deliver-request@1: a first-party service puts a result of the person's own work into their Vibe chats (OpenVibe.Actor: each finished run of one of their OpenVibe Agents, when the agent sends its results to Vibe). Chat keeps one chat per source, named after it, and posts the text there as Vibe's message, so each run is a chat they can open and continue. No AI answer is made and nothing counts against their allowance. POST /internal/chat/vibe/deliver, capability chat.vibe.deliver, loopback only.

subject.description: The person whose work it is, as the calling service vouches (Actor: the agent's owner).

id.description: The source's stable id (the agent's agt_ id): one chat per source.

name.description: What to call it in the chat's name (the agent's name).

text.description: The result, in Markdown (as Vibe's answers are shown).

url.description: Where the whole run is (its steps, sources and cost).

idempotency_key.description: The caller's id for this result (Actor: the run's task id): sent again, it is posted once.

chat.vibe-deliver-result.v1.title: ChatVibeDeliverResult
chat.vibe-deliver-result.v1.description: chat.vibe-deliver-result@1: where a chat.vibe-deliver-request@1 was posted. `repeated` is true when the idempotency key was seen before (nothing was posted again).

common.owned-resource-control-request.v1.title: OwnedResourceControlRequest
common.owned-resource-control-request.v1.description: common.owned-resource-control-request@1 (ADR-048 amendment 2026-10-15, step 8 phase 2): one control operation on a person-owned resource. Robots, chat rooms, restream definitions and pastes belong to a person, not to a project, so they carry no OVRN and the project-scoped common.resource-control-request@1 cannot name them. OpenVibe.Services sends this to the owning authority's POST /api/v1/resources/control (the same route, told apart by `owned`), acting for the person in on_behalf_of. owned names the resource by its index summary's kind and id. owner is the person it belongs to: the authority refuses unless its own record says the same (Services also offers actions only on the viewer's own resources). A sensitive action (deleting, physical control) asked by an agent is refused with confirmation_required until the owner approves, as for project resources. idempotency_key makes a retry safe: the authority answers a repeated key from the same caller with the first result, and refuses the key reused with another request. Answered with common.resource-control-result@1 (without resource: there is no OVRN). The actions each authority takes are in its <service>.resource.control capability; any other action is refused unsupported.

owned.description: The resource, as its owning authority's resource index lists it (common.resource-summary@1 kind and id).

id.description: The summary's id: a prefixed ULID (rob_…) or the service's own slug (a paste, a room).

owner.description: The person the resource belongs to. Person-owned resources belong to people, never to agents or apps.

params.description: Action-specific input, shaped by the authority's own contract (never redefined here).

on_behalf_of.description: Who asks: the owner, or their agent (whose sensitive actions wait for the owner's approval).

confirmation_id.description: The approved confirmation from an earlier confirmation_required answer.

common.resource-control-result.v1.title: ResourceControlResult
common.resource-control-result.v1.description: common.resource-control-result@1: the authority's answer to a common.resource-control-request@1 (ADR-048, plan T13). state is the outcome, not the resource's own state: done (applied), pending (accepted and asynchronous; the authority reports completion later on its events), refused (a policy or confirmation gate said no) or failed (an error). State rules: refused carries problem or confirmation_required; failed carries problem; done and pending carry neither; confirmation_required appears only on refused. result carries the authority's own response document and never another service's rows. The state rules are checked by contracts.resources.checkControlResult.

confirmation_required.description: The action needs its owner's approval; retry the same request with this confirmation_id once approved.

problem.description: RFC 9457 body when refused or failed.

common.resource-list-result.v1.title: ResourceListResult
common.resource-list-result.v1.description: A page of the resource index (roadmap WS-Z7).

partial.description: Authorities a merged index (OpenVibe.Services, ADR-048) could not read for this page: a slow or failing authority is omitted, never fails the page. Each entry names the authority and the problem code it answered. Added in 1.1.0; a single authority's own index leaves it out.

common.resource-name.v1.title: ResourceName
common.resource-name.v1.description: common.resource-name@1: the one stable, cross-service name of an OpenVibe resource (OVRN; ADR-034 section 2, ADR-048, plan T13): ovrn:<service>:<project_id>:<type>/<id>, for example ovrn:media:prj_01J0000000000000000000000A:object/med_01K0000000000000000000000B. The service segment is the authority that owns the resource; the project segment is its tenancy boundary; type is the second half of a common.resource-summary@1 kind and id is that summary's id, so the name composes from any resource summary. It is used in grant scopes, audit rows, event subjects, usage records, bill lines and console URLs. It never names a person, an app, a request, a session or an event. The pattern is the one common.usage-recorded@1 resource and common.resource-summary@1 ovrn already use.

common.resource-summary.v1.title: ResourceSummary
common.resource-summary.v1.description: One resource of any service, as the resource index lists it (roadmap WS-Z7): every service answers GET /api/v1/resources with these, so OpenVibe.Services shows any resource without owning its data.

kind.description: service.kind, e.g. watch.watch, actor.actor, media.object, events.subscription

ovrn.description: Optional resource name (ADR-034 section 2), the name grants, audit, events, usage records and bills use: ovrn:<service>:<project_id>:<type>/<id>, e.g. ovrn:watch:<project_id>:watch/<wch_id>, with the pattern of common.usage-recorded@1 resource. Its service, project and id are this summary's service, project_id and id. Added in 1.1.0.

errors.problem.v1.title: Problem
errors.problem.v1.description: RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json) with a stable OpenVibe error code and trace identifiers. The legacy 'error' string is allowed during migration so existing clients keep working.

error.description: Deprecated compatibility field: same text as title/detail for clients that read {error}.

identity.subject-ref.v1.title: SubjectRef
identity.subject-ref.v1.description: The one cross-platform reference to an actor. Issued by OpenVibe.Network. Never a service-local integer id.

oneOf.description: AgentSubject: an agent (OpenVibe.Actor, or a developer app's agent) acting under grants its owner delegated (roadmap WS-Z2). In an event envelope, on_behalf_of names the owner.

openvibeToken.description: An OpenVibe Network token for this service: a person's token, an app token (client credentials, audience of the service) or a first-party service token. Its `cap` claim must include the capability the operation names.
